newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods trim gains at close, diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods trim gains at close, diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. spot products trimmed much of their earlier gains ahead of the futures close Thursday, as NYMEX gave back much of its morning gains but differentials held onto their earlier trends, traders said.
Gasoline prices were still from 0.50 cent to over 1.50 cents a gallon higher by dint of firmer differentials both in New York Harbor (NYH) and at the U.S. Gulf (USG).

Heavy buying in NYH led by Tosco on Wednesday kept diffs hot, with prompt "M5" and "A5" regular winter-grade conventional and reformulated blends heard talked 0.50 cent firmer at 3.00 and 4.00 cents over Dec NYMEX respectively.

Gulf Coast gasoline prices also moved out, with diffs on the newly-prompt back 32nd Colonial Pipeline scheduling cycle firming to about 2.50 cents over Dec futures from assessments early Thursday at 1.00 cent over. Traders said solid buying, some possibly linked to reports of problems at Amoco's Texas City, Texas refinery, cited. Amoco declined to comment.

On the distillate front, prices were about 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon firmer amid softness on diffs for both USG diesel and NYH heating oil. Traders said pipelines into the midcontinent from Houston were full and leaving some barrels in Houston without a place to go, which softened diffs.
Prompt diesel in Houston was heard done at 1.20 cents under December NYMEX, with bids slipping to even weaker levels, traders said.
They also said heating oil supply was now exceeding supply in the huge East Coast heat oil market. Prompt NYH 86-grade heating oil was heard offered at 0.25 cent under December NYMEX, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
